title: Checks for the use of __metaclass__ = type in class definitions.
summary: Since Python 3, __metaclass__ = type is implied and can thus be omitted. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.155.

title: Checks for uses of type that take a primitive as an argument.
summary: type() returns the type of a given object. A type of a primitive can always be known in advance and accessed directly, which is more concise and explicit than using type(). Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.155.

title: Checks for classes that inherit from object.
summary: Since Python 3, all classes inherit from object by default, so object can be omitted from the list of base classes. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.155.

title: Checks for uses of deprecated methods from the unittest module.
summary: The unittest module has deprecated aliases for some of its methods. The deprecated aliases were removed in Python 3.12. Instead of aliases, use their non-deprecated counterparts. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.155.

title: Checks for the use of generics that can be replaced with standard library variants based on PEP 585.
summary: PEP 585 enabled collections in the Python standard library (like list) to be used as generics directly, instead of importing analogous members from the typing module (like typing.List). Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.155.
message_templates: Use `{}` instead of `{}` for type annotation

title: Check for type annotations that can be rewritten based on PEP 604 syntax.
summary: PEP 604 introduced a new syntax for union type annotations based on the | operator. This syntax is more concise and readable than the previous typing.Union and typing.Optional syntaxes. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.155.

title: Checks for super calls that pass redundant arguments.
summary: In Python 3, super can be invoked without any arguments when: (1) the first argument is __class__, and (2) the second argument is equivalent to the first argument of the enclosing method. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.155.

title: Checks for unnecessary UTF-8 encoding declarations.
summary: PEP 3120 makes UTF-8 the default encoding, so a UTF-8 encoding declaration is unnecessary. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.155.

title: Checks for unnecessary __future__ imports.
summary: The __future__ module is used to enable features that are not yet available in the current Python version. If a feature is already available in the minimum supported Python version, importing it from __future__ is unnecessary and should be removed to avoid confusion. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.155.
message_templates: Unnecessary `__future__` import `{}` for target Python version
Unnecessary `__future__` imports {} for target Python version

title: Checks for unnecessary parentheses on functools.lru_cache decorators.
summary: Since Python 3.8, functools.lru_cache can be used as a decorator without trailing parentheses, as long as no arguments are passed to it. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.155.

title: Checks for unnecessary calls to encode as UTF-8.
summary: UTF-8 is the default encoding in Python, so there is no need to call encode when UTF-8 is the desired encoding. Instead, use a bytes literal. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.155.

title: Checks for TypedDict declarations that use functional syntax.
summary: TypedDict types can be defined either through a functional syntax (Foo = TypedDict(...)) or a class syntax (class Foo(TypedDict): ...). Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.155.
message_templates: Convert `{}` from `TypedDict` functional to class syntax

title: Checks for NamedTuple declarations that use functional syntax.
summary: NamedTuple subclasses can be defined either through a functional syntax (Foo = NamedTuple(...)) or a class syntax (class Foo(NamedTuple): ...). Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.155.
message_templates: Convert `{}` from `NamedTuple` functional to class syntax

title: Checks for redundant open mode arguments.
summary: Redundant open mode arguments are unnecessary and should be removed to avoid confusion. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.155.

title: Checks for uses of datetime.timezone.utc.
summary: As of Python 3.11, datetime.UTC is an alias for datetime.timezone.utc. The alias is more readable and generally preferred over the full path. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.192.

title: Checks for unnecessary calls to str, bytes, int, float, bool, and complex.
summary: The mentioned constructors can be replaced with their respective literal forms, which are more readable and idiomatic. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.193.

title: Checks for uses of typing.Text and typing_extensions.Text.
summary: typing.Text is an alias for str, and only exists for Python 2 compatibility. As of Python 3.11, typing.Text is deprecated. Use str instead. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.195.

title: Checks for uses of io.open.
summary: In Python 3, io.open is an alias for open. Prefer using open directly, as it is more idiomatic. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.196.

title: Checks for uses of subprocess.run that set the universal_newlines keyword argument.
summary: As of Python 3.7, the universal_newlines keyword argument has been renamed to text, and now exists for backwards compatibility. The universal_newlines keyword argument may be removed in a future version of Python. Prefer text, which is more explicit and readable. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.196.

title: Checks for uses of subprocess.run that send stdout and stderr to a pipe.
summary: As of Python 3.7, subprocess.run has a capture_output keyword argument that can be set to True to capture stdout and stderr outputs. This is equivalent to setting stdout and stderr to subprocess.PIPE, but is more explicit and readable. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.199.

title: Checks for uses of the xml.etree.cElementTree module.
summary: In Python 3.3, xml.etree.cElementTree was deprecated in favor of xml.etree.ElementTree. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.199.

title: Checks for uses of exceptions that alias OSError.
summary: OSError is the builtin error type used for exceptions that relate to the operating system. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.206.

title: Checks for uses of the Unicode kind prefix (u) in strings.
summary: In Python 3, all strings are Unicode by default. The Unicode kind prefix is unnecessary and should be removed to avoid confusion. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.201.

title: Checks for imports of the mock module that should be replaced with unittest.mock.
summary: Since Python 3.3, mock has been a part of the standard library as unittest.mock. The mock package is deprecated; use unittest.mock instead. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.206.

title: Checks for list comprehensions that are immediately unpacked.
summary: There is no reason to use a list comprehension if the result is immediately unpacked. Instead, use a generator expression, which avoids allocating an intermediary list. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade, and removed it.
message_templates: Replace unpacked list comprehension with a generator expression

title: Checks for for loops that can be replaced with yield from expressions.
summary: If a for loop only contains a yield statement, it can be replaced with a yield from expression, which is more concise and idiomatic. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.210.

title: Checks for imports of Python 3 builtins from Python 2 compatibility shims such as python-future and six.
summary: These shims existed to access Python 3 builtins from code that also ran on Python 2. On Python 3-only code, the imports are redundant. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.211.

title: Checks for unnecessary positional indices in format strings.
summary: In Python 3.1 and later, format strings can use implicit positional references. For example, "{0}, {1}".format("Hello", "World") can be rewritten as "{}, {}".format("Hello", "World"). Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.218.
message_templates: Use implicit references for positional format fields

title: Checks for printf-style string formatting, and offers to replace it with str.format calls.
summary: printf-style string formatting has a number of quirks, and leads to less readable code than using str.format calls or f-strings. In general, prefer the newer str.format and f-strings constructs over printf-style string formatting. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.229.
message_templates: Use format specifiers instead of percent format

title: Checks for str.format calls that can be replaced with f-strings.
summary: f-strings are more readable and generally preferred over str.format calls. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.224.

title: Checks for uses of functools.lru_cache that set maxsize=None.
summary: Since Python 3.9, functools.cache can be used as a drop-in replacement for functools.lru_cache(maxsize=None). When possible, prefer functools.cache as it is more readable and idiomatic. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.225.

title: Checks for extraneous parentheses.
summary: Extraneous parentheses are redundant, and can be removed to improve readability while retaining identical semantics. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.228.

title: Checks for uses of deprecated imports based on the minimum supported Python version.
summary: Deprecated imports may be removed in future versions of Python, and should be replaced with their new equivalents. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.239.

title: Checks for conditional blocks gated on sys.version_info comparisons that are outdated for the minimum supported Python version.
summary: In Python, code can be conditionally executed based on the active Python version by comparing against the sys.version_info tuple. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.240.
message_templates: Version block is outdated for minimum Python version

title: Checks for the presence of unnecessary quotes in type annotations.
summary: In Python, type annotations can be quoted to avoid forward references. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.242.

title: Checks for uses of isinstance and issubclass that take a tuple of types for comparison.
summary: Since Python 3.10, isinstance and issubclass can be passed a |-separated union of types, which is consistent with the union operator introduced in PEP 604. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade, and removed it.
message_templates: Use `X | Y` in `{}` call instead of `(X, Y)`

title: Checks for class definitions that include unnecessary parentheses after the class name.
summary: If a class definition doesn't have any bases, the parentheses are unnecessary. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.273.

title: Checks for use of TypeAlias annotations and TypeAliasType assignments for declaring type aliases.
summary: The type keyword was introduced in Python 3.12 by PEP 695 for defining type aliases. The type keyword is easier to read and provides cleaner support for generics. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.0.283.
message_templates: Type alias `{}` uses {} instead of the `type` keyword

title: Checks for uses of exceptions that alias TimeoutError.
summary: TimeoutError is the builtin error type used for exceptions when a system function timed out at the system level. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in v0.2.0.

title: Checks for classes that inherit from both str and enum.Enum.
summary: Python 3.11 introduced enum.StrEnum, which is preferred over inheriting from both str and enum.Enum. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in 0.15.0.

title: Checks for unnecessary default type arguments for Generator and AsyncGenerator on Python 3.13+.
summary: Python 3.13 introduced the ability for type parameters to specify default values. Following this change, several standard-library classes were updated to add default values for some of their type parameters. For example, Generatorint is now equivalent to Generatorint, None, None, as the second and third type parameters of Generator now default to None. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in 0.8.0.

title: Checks for uses of Unpack[] on Python 3.11 and above, and suggests using * instead.
summary: PEP 646 introduced a new syntax for unpacking sequences based on the * operator. This syntax is more concise and readable than the previous Unpack[] syntax. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in 0.10.0.

title: Check for typing.Optional annotations that can be rewritten based on PEP 604 syntax.
summary: PEP 604 introduced a new syntax for union type annotations based on the | operator. This syntax is more concise and readable than the previous typing.Optional syntax. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in 0.12.0.

title: Checks for use of standalone type variables and parameter specifications in generic classes.
summary: Special type parameter syntax was introduced in Python 3.12 by PEP 695 for defining generic classes. This syntax is easier to read and provides cleaner support for generics. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in 0.12.0.
message_templates: Generic class `{}` uses `Generic` subclass instead of type parameters

title: Checks for use of standalone type variables and parameter specifications in generic functions.
summary: Special type parameter syntax was introduced in Python 3.12 by PEP 695 for defining generic functions. This syntax is easier to read and provides cleaner support for generics. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in 0.12.0.
message_templates: Generic function `{}` should use type parameters

title: Checks for while loops that use 1 as their condition.
summary: while 1: is a Python 2 idiom, where True was a global that could be rebound and so had to be loaded and tested on every iteration. In Python 3 True is a keyword, so both spellings compile to the same bytecode and while True: is clearer about the loop being infinite. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade. It is in preview.

title: Checks for use of PEP 695 type parameters with leading underscores in generic classes and functions.
summary: PEP 695 type parameters are already restricted in scope to the class or function in which they appear, so leading underscores just hurt readability without the usual privacy benefits. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in 0.12.0.

title: Checks for metaclass=type in class definitions.
summary: Since Python 3, the default metaclass is type, so specifying it explicitly is redundant. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade and made it stable in 0.13.0.

title: Checks for uses of abstractclassmethod, abstractstaticmethod, abstractproperty.
summary: These have been deprecated since Python 3.3 and are expected to be removed in a future version of Python. Ruff takes this rule from pyupgrade. It is in preview.
